text: The retention period is a parameter row of the rwb-case parameter catalog per product group, read at run time through the parameters contract of DP-06, and the retention timer type is a new row of LOV-TIMER; the length of the period and the code of the timer type are set at reference-data load and not in this story.
why: R-WO-36 starts the retention timer and R-WO-47 fires on its expiry, but no source read for this work package states the length of the retention period and LOV-TIMER holds no retention timer type; a value written in code would break BR-S7-013 and the guardrail that no business value sits in code.
read: Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 R-WO-36 and R-WO-47; FSD S7 v3 A2.13; LDM v8 DF-WRK-030 and LOV-TIMER; Template and Rules R5.5 DP-06 and DP-07
confirm: Parameter and reference-data load before wave 4; rwb-case reference-data owner (RW-COE)
impact: No value is fixed in code; the expiry of every case is computed from the row in force at the start of the retention period

text: The retention-start answer of R-WO-36 and the closure decision of R-WO-47 are the two operations of RWB-S7-E6025-CON; rwb-writeoff pushes the retention-start answer, and the closure step of rwb-case asks rwb-writeoff for the closure decision when the retention durable timer fires. Paths, methods and element names are fixed by that contract story.
why: The legacy story names only the write-off service's endpoints and the sources give no transport for the two answers, while the retention timer is a row of rwb-case and its expiry has to produce the closure question somewhere.
read: RWB-E6-025 endpoints and AC2 and AC3; Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 R-WO-36 and R-WO-47 (Workbench scheduler, Document Hub, Decision Log); TSD P3 v3 T2.3 and T2.4; Template and Rules R5.5 DP-11
confirm: Contract review of RWB-S7-E6025-CON and the rwb-writeoff API specification
impact: Renames and re-homes the calls if the contract differs; no rule, criterion or test changes

text: The guard facts of R-WO-47 - no open placement, no open sale, no open exception and a retention class on every document - are evaluated by rwb-writeoff and rwb-document and arrive in the closure answer as a Close or Hold decision; rwb-case checks only its own open actions, which are a task in status OPEN and a timer other than the retention timer in status RUNNING.
why: The four guard facts belong to rwb-partner, rwb-debtsale, rwb-deviation and rwb-document, and a service may not read another service's tables or chain calls; the case-side reading of the legacy criterion no action is open has to be the case's own tasks and timers.
read: Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 R-WO-47 and R-WO-48; RWB-E6-025 AC1 and AC3; FSD P3 v4 AC-EXC-P3-050-03; Template and Rules R5.5 DP-01
confirm: Architecture review of the write-off route set and the rwb-document retention class contract
impact: Moves no rule out of S7; fixes what the case side checks before it applies a Close answer

text: A retention closure writes the closure reason WRITTEN_OFF of LOV-CLOSURE on the case, and the case status moves to closed with the stage.
why: DF-CAS-023 offers eight LOV-CLOSURE values and FEAT-WOF-13 names none of them; a charge-off closed after its retention period is the written-off case of that list and no other value fits.
read: LDM v8 DF-CAS-023 and LOV-CLOSURE values CURED, SETTLED, REALIZED, SOLD, WRITTEN_OFF, INSURANCE_SETTLED, MERGED, CANCELED; FSD S7 v3 A2.13
confirm: Reference-data review of LOV-CLOSURE by the rwb-case reference-data owner
impact: The stored value is a reference row; if the list changes, the row changes and no code changes

text: SCR-27 shows the closed case with the state Closed, its closing date, its closure reason and its stopped timers, read only, and the field order, the masking and the merge order of the composite route are set at the edge review; the write-off facts of the screen come from rwb-writeoff on the same route.
why: The legacy screen row names SCR-27 and its four states and says nothing of a closed display or of field order, and the screen is composed by the gateway-bff in the target.
read: RWB-E6-025 screen and states block; FSD S7 v3 A2.13; Template and Rules R5.5 DP-19; Architecture v5 slide 10
confirm: Edge and UX review of SCR-27 at wave 4
impact: Layout only; no field, rule or criterion changes

text: The Epics 3 to 8 story RWB-E6-025 carries no requirement ID, so this story claims none; the feature-level requirement REQ-S7-008 states the behaviour and stays with the S7 slice RWB-S7-E6025-APP.
why: The legacy story has no requirement row and the only requirement that names the behaviour is the write-off module requirement, which the S7 slice owns.
read: RWB-E6-025 metadata table; FSD S7 v3 requirement table REQ-S7-008; FSD P3 v4 document control
confirm: Traceability review at the end of the stage
impact: No requirement is duplicated across the two slices of the key
